_comment: Fragment 7 — tooling provenance and graph durability. Merged 2026-08-20. Closes G50, G51, G52, G53; records D-51 and the deferred G54/G55.

nodes.label: Graph Fragments — Curated Layer
nodes.description: Tooling documentation, outside the D-29 tier stack. Records which graphify distribution is installed and why, the nine distribution-specific commands, the rebuild order for the curated layer, the four-step merge verification, and the deferred G54 validation route. Holds the fragment set that the curated layer rebuilds from; totals are computed, not restated.
nodes.rationale: Created 2026-08-20 to close G50, G51, and G52. Explicitly not a fourth v1 document — it records no decision, gap disposition, build order, or artifact status.

nodes.label: D-51 — Graphify Distribution Standardised
nodes.description: The project standardises on @sentropic/graphify (npm). Upstream graphifyy (PyPI) is not adopted, and a swap is gated on G54 closing first. Classified Project Scope, infrastructure-owned, outside the D-29 tier stack: generates no FR, no AC, no SPECS candidate.
nodes.rationale: Three grounds in descending hardness: the upstream path is not installable here (no uv, pipx, or pip; python resolves to the Microsoft Store stub), it would invalidate nine mandated commands, and it moves backwards into the graphify-out layout the rules call legacy.

nodes.label: Attributed Downstream Extension
nodes.description: The relation between Graphify-Labs/graphify (upstream, PyPI graphifyy, Python) and rhanka/graphify (npm @sentropic/graphify, TypeScript). The downstream credits the upstream by name and tracks parity in UPSTREAM_GAP.md. Neither repo redirects to the other. The upstream's not-affiliated warning is scoped to PyPI and says nothing about npm.
nodes.rationale: The seventh instance of the naming-difference error family. A different repo, language, and package name read as a provenance problem; it is a distribution relationship. Recorded so the install is not repeatedly re-litigated.

nodes.label: Curated Graph Layer — Not Rebuildable
nodes.description: The graph has two layers. The extracted layer rebuilds from docs/. The curated layer does not — it rebuilds only from docs/graph-fragments/. Extraction does not regenerate curation. Counts are deliberately not restated here; compute them from the fragments, because a hard-coded total is wrong the next time anything merges.
nodes.rationale: G51. Before 2026-08-20 the curated layer existed only in session-scoped temp storage while .gitignore asserted the graph was rebuildable from docs/. That claim was false and load-bearing: it is the sentence that makes deleting the graph look safe.

nodes.label: Shared Core Across Agent Rule Files
nodes.description: One byte-identical rule core carried by CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .agents/rules/graphify.md, plus a declared platform tail that legitimately differs. Change all three together or none. The first concrete instance of the G11 arbitration rule.
nodes.rationale: G53. Not all the drift was defect: the Codex $graphify lines and the Gemini skill path are correct for their platforms. The real defect was the absence of a shared core, plus an abbreviated migrate-state rule in .agents — the G32 pattern in the tooling layer.

nodes.label: Tooling Provenance Audit 2026-08-20
nodes.description: Audit triggered by a challenge to whether @sentropic/graphify was the correct install. Validated the install as correct and surfaced two larger problems than the one asked about: the curated layer was unreproducible (G51) and three agent rule blocks had drifted (G53).
nodes.rationale: Third audit section in the register, alongside the 2026-08-19 consistency audit and the repo-creation drift audit.

nodes.label: G54 — Upstream Command Surface Unverified
nodes.description: Open by decision, not oversight. Whether the upstream CLI truly lacks the nine distribution-specific commands rests on a README reading, not a verified command list. Route: install a Python toolchain, install graphifyy alongside without uninstalling npm, diff graphify --help, record the result as a decision.
nodes.rationale: Guaranteed to fail: uninstalling npm before verifying. If upstream lacks merge-graphs and build --fragment, the curated layer cannot be re-merged by the remaining tool — the fragments survive but nothing installed can consume them. Coexistence is cheap; recovery is not.

nodes.label: G55 — Disposition Table Stops at G39
nodes.description: G40 through G49 are absent from the §5.1 all-IDs disposition table. All ten are recorded elsewhere in the register, but the index that claims to carry every ID does not reach them. Only G40 is genuinely bare; G49 has treatment under a heading not keyed to its ID. The third recurrence of the disposition-drift pattern, now at a scale of ten.
nodes.rationale: Recorded, not repaired — the backfill was outside approved scope, and adding G50–G54 rows to a table missing G40–G49 would make it look complete while it is not. The table now names its own incompleteness. An artifact honest about its gap is safe; one that hides it is not.

nodes.label: Curated Update Is a Merge, Not a Build
nodes.description: graphify build --fragment builds; it does not merge. graph.json stores relationships under links; fragments declare them under edges. Copying edges across unchanged produces degree-zero orphan nodes: present, findable by explain, reachable by nothing. It fails silently.
nodes.rationale: The reason every curated update in this project has gone through a merge script. The path traversal check in the four-step verification is what catches the orphan failure.
